h1: The 8 Best 49-Inch Ultrawide Monitors of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best 49-inch ultrawide monitors of 2026, covering QD-OLED, VA and IPS Black options for gaming and work desks.
summary: The MSI MPG 491CQP is the best overall for QD-OLED at the lowest entry price here. The Samsung Odyssey G93SC is the proven premium pick, the G91SD adds HDMI 2.1, the G95C is the brightest, and the Dell U4924DW and Samsung S95UA are the productivity picks.
intro: A 49 inch ultrawide is roughly two 27 inch monitors fused into one, but the number that trips buyers is not the size, it is the 5120 by 1440 resolution. That is a lot of width and only 1440 pixels of height, so text is sharper than on a 1080p pair but not as crisp as 4K. Plan for the desk depth too.

We reviewed eight 49 inch ultrawides on paper, comparing panel type, refresh rate, brightness, connectivity and warranty. Every pick here sits in the $500 and up tier, so ranking focuses on what you get at that level.

products.name: MSI MPG 491CQP QD-OLED
products.verdict: QD-OLED contrast at the lowest entry price here.
products.description:
This 49 inch QD-OLED has a 5120 by 1440 resolution, 144Hz refresh, 0.03ms response, FreeSync Premium Pro, USB-C and a tilt and height adjustable stand, with a 2 year warranty.

It ranks first because it brings QD-OLED, with deep blacks, at the lowest entry price in the guide. The Samsung G93SC runs 240Hz and has a longer warranty, but costs more.

Buy it for mixed gaming and work. The 2 year warranty is a year shorter than Samsung's, which matters on OLED.

products.name: Samsung Odyssey G93SC
products.description:
The G93SC is a 49 inch curved 1800R QD-OLED at 5120 by 1440 and 240Hz with 0.03ms response. Samsung quotes a million to one contrast and 99% DCI-P3 color coverage, and it supports both G-Sync and FreeSync Premium Pro plus PbP, with 3 years of coverage.

It ranks second because it is faster than the MSI and has a longer warranty, but costs more in a tier where all picks are expensive.

Choose it for fast games and color work. A curved screen does take a deep desk.

products.name: Samsung Odyssey G9 G91SD
products.verdict: QD-OLED with HDMI 2.1 and a metal build.
products.description:
The G91SD is a 49 inch QD-OLED at 5120 by 1440, 144Hz, 0.03ms GtG, with FreeSync Premium Pro, G-Sync compatibility, HDMI 2.1, USB-C, PbP, a metal design and a 3 year warranty.

It ranks third because 144Hz trails the G93SC, but HDMI 2.1 lets consoles run at higher frame rates.

Pick it if a console shares the desk.

products.name: Samsung Odyssey G9 G91F
products.verdict: A curved VA with DisplayHDR 600 and auto source switching.
products.description:
The G91F is a 49 inch curved 1000R VA at 5120 by 1440. It refreshes at 144Hz with 1ms response, peaks near 280 nits for DisplayHDR 600, and adds FreeSync Premium Pro, PbP and automatic input switching, backed by 3 years of coverage.

It ranks fourth because VA lacks OLED black levels, but it avoids OLED burn in concerns.

Buy it if you prefer VA and mixed use.

products.name: Samsung Odyssey G9 G95C
products.verdict: 1000 nit peak brightness, the highest here.
products.description:
The G95C is a 49 inch curved 1000R VA at 5120 by 1440, 240Hz, 1ms GtG, with 1000 nit peak brightness, the highest in this guide, FreeSync Premium Pro and PbP.

It ranks fifth because VA cannot match QD-OLED contrast, even if it is brighter.

Choose it for bright rooms and HDR highlights.

products.name: Samsung Odyssey G9 G95SD
products.verdict: The only pick with a glare free coating.
products.description:
The G95SD is a 49 inch QD-OLED with a glare free coating, 5120 by 1440, 240Hz, 0.03ms GtG, built in Wi-Fi, SmartThings and a Gaming Hub for streaming games without a PC, plus a 3 year warranty.

It ranks sixth because buyer feedback is the weakest of the group, though the coating helps bright rooms.

Buy it if reflections bother you.

products.name: Dell UltraSharp U4924DW
products.verdict: A productivity monitor with an automatic KVM.
products.description:
The Dell U4924DW is a 49 inch IPS Black at 5120 by 1440, 60Hz, with an automatic KVM switch, USB-C with 90W power delivery, 2.5GbE Ethernet, 11 USB ports, dual 9W speakers and 100% sRGB.

It ranks seventh because 60Hz is the lowest here, but it is the best for multi computer desks.

Buy it for work, not gaming.

products.name: Samsung Business S95UA
products.verdict: A built in KVM at a lower price than the Dell.
products.description:
The S95UA is a 49 inch curved 1000R VA at 5120 by 1440 and 120Hz, with a built in KVM, USB-C with 90W power delivery, Ethernet, speakers, DisplayHDR 400 and a business 3 year warranty.

It ranks last because HDR and panel are modest, but it undercuts the Dell and runs at 120Hz.

Pick it for an office desk on a tighter budget.

whatMatters.detail: QD-OLED gives deep blacks, VA gives high brightness and IPS Black gives accurate color. OLED can show burn in over time, so warranty matters. Check the panel name in the title.
5120 by 1440 is like two 2560 by 1440 screens side by side. It is wide but not 4K tall. Confirm the pixel count.
Higher refresh feels smoother in games. 60Hz is fine for office use. Check the Hz figure.
A KVM lets two computers share one keyboard and mouse. USB-C with 90W charges a laptop. Look for these in the specs.
A tighter curve like 1000R wraps more but needs depth. Keep about 28 inches of desk depth. Check curve numbers.

cards.label: QD-OLED
cards.text: Deep blacks and fast response. MSI 491CQP, G93SC, G91SD and G95SD use it.

cards.label: VA
cards.text: Brighter peaks and no burn in worry. G91F, G95C and S95UA use it.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to QD-OLED unless the room is very bright.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: USB-C with 90W power delivery, a KVM and Ethernet.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: Dell UltraSharp U4924DW and Samsung Business S95UA both offer 90W USB-C and Ethernet.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want speed and a longer warranty. Samsung Odyssey G93SC has 240Hz and 3 years.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want OLED for less. The MSI MPG 491CQP is the entry point.

faq.a: A 49 inch is about 45 inches wide. Measure your desk width and depth.
Expecting 4K sharpness. 5120 by 1440 is wide but not tall.

faq.q: Is QD-OLED worth it over VA?
faq.a: For contrast, yes. MSI's QD-OLED costs the least among OLEDs here.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Use DisplayPort for full refresh. The G91SD also offers HDMI 2.1.

faq.q: How do I limit burn in?
faq.a: Vary static content and use screen savers, and note the warranty.
Yes, the Dell U4924DW and Samsung S95UA include a KVM.

finalTake: The MSI MPG 491CQP is the best entry to QD-OLED, and the Samsung G93SC is the premium choice. Pick the Dell U4924DW for office KVM work. Measure the desk, then decide gaming or work.
